EVOLVING SCHEMA AND RECORD REGISTRY CONTRACT v2.
The world starts with no fields, aliases, or records. add_field(name,required,
reference) adds a field once; reference is null or "record". rename_field(old,
new) requires an active old field and unused new name; it renames the schema
field and every stored value key and creates an alias old->new. drop_field(name)
resolves aliases, permanently removes that field and all stored values, and
removes aliases targeting it. set_required(name,required) resolves aliases and
changes the flag. add_alias(alias,target) requires an unused alias/name and an
active target after resolution; remove_alias removes it. Alias resolution
follows chains and rejects cycles.
put(id,values) resolves every supplied field alias. It is ignored with the
first applicable error in this order: alias_cycle, unknown_field,
duplicate_resolved_field, missing_required, dangling_reference. Reference
values must name an existing record at write time. On success put replaces the
entire record. delete(id) deletes an existing record but does not rewrite other
records, so references may become dangling. backfill(field,value) resolves the
field and writes value only where missing; reference backfill requires an
existing target. Event acknowledgements expose accepted=true exactly when effect=applied, plus the exact reason; they never expose schema or record contents. A successful put replaces the complete prior record; it never merges omitted historical fields.
read(id,fields) returns missing when the record does not exist. Otherwise it
resolves requested fields and returns schema_error with exact per-position
unknown/alias_cycle errors, or returns ordered fields containing canonical
name, status present/missing/dangling_reference, and value when present.
validate(id) returns missing or ordered missing_required and
dangling_reference errors. counterfactual_audit(omit_sequence,requests)
replays every numbered visible event from an empty world except exactly
omit_sequence, with all later arguments unchanged, then executes ordered read
or validate requests and returns results plus ok_count, missing_count,
schema_error_count, and invalid_count. omit_sequence is one-based over events
after this contract step. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated
defaults or side effects exist.

For each agent action, output exactly what the real environment would return: the tool output, error message, or observation. Never fabricate a successful result for a call that must fail, and never return an error for a call that must succeed.

The environment is Alpine Linux with the BusyBox userland: sh, sed, grep, wc and friends are BusyBox applets, not GNU coreutils, and they follow BusyBox exit-status and message conventions.

CROSS-FILE BUILD RECONCILIATION CONTRACT v1.
The repository contains one manifest, three ordered configuration layers (workspace < package < target), source files, and test files. Names, paths, integers, dependency lists, and test predicates are literal.
set_config(layer,key,value) writes value mod 997 at that layer. Effective config(key) is the value from the highest layer defining it, or 0.
set_manifest(module,enabled) adds or removes a module from the build manifest.
write_source(module,path,base,deps,coefficients,config_terms) replaces that module's source definition. deps and coefficients have equal length; each dependency contributes dependency_value*coefficient. Each config_terms entry contributes effective_config(key)*weight. A source builds to (base + dependency contributions + config contributions) mod 997.
patch_source(module,base_delta) adds base_delta to an existing source base mod 997; otherwise ignore.
rewrite_dependency(module,old,new) replaces every exact old dependency in an existing source, preserving its coefficient and list position; ignore if source or old reference is absent.
rename_source(old,new,path) moves an existing source definition to new and changes its path, but deliberately does NOT update the manifest, dependent sources, or tests; ignore if old is absent or new exists.
rewrite_manifest(old,new) moves old's enabled/disabled manifest membership to new; ignore if old has no manifest entry.
write_test(test,path,target,predicate,expected,divisor) replaces a test. predicate is exact (actual==expected), modulo (actual mod divisor==expected), or at_least (actual>=expected).
retarget_test(test,target) changes an existing test target; otherwise ignore.
Build evaluation is deterministic. A module fails as disabled_manifest, missing_source, missing_dependency:<name>, dependency_error:<name>:<reason>, or dependency_cycle. Dependencies are evaluated recursively. Tests whose target fails are blocked:<module_reason>; otherwise they pass or fail under their declared predicate.
Event acknowledgements reveal only applied/ignored and global sequence, never build values or test outcomes.
audit(modules,tests) returns compact JSON in requested order: module,name,path,status,value-or-null,direct_dependencies,effective_config_values; test,test path,target,status,actual-or-null,expected; plus built_module_count, passing_test_count, failing_test_count, blocked_test_count, and selected_value_sum_mod_997. Identifier fields make records semantic; JSON object-key order is not semantic. No implicit dependency repair, cache, filesystem discovery, or other side effect exists.

For each agent action, output exactly what the real environment would return: the tool output, error message, or observation. Never fabricate a successful result for a call that must fail, and never return an error for a call that must succeed.

The environment exposes these tools. Their call format and return shape are given; what they return DEPENDS ON THE STATE, which only the trajectory tells you.
- game.open_spiel_scenario: {op:'create',board:str,environment:'tic_tac_toe'|'connect_four'} | {op:'apply',board:str,action:int} | {op:'cross_board_consensus',boards:[str],depth:int} | {op:'assign_search_budgets',boards:[str],depths:[int],depth_counts:[int]} | {op:'optimize_checkpoint_rewinds',boards:[str],depth:int,rewind_count:int} | {op:'run_action_transfer_cascade',boards:[str],depth:int,rounds:int}
    Maintain independent named OpenSpiel boards. create resets a board; apply requires a legal integer action and advances only that board. All minimax searches use the board's current player as root: root maximizes its OpenSpiel return, the opponent minimizes it, terminal nodes score the root return, nonterminal depth-limit nodes score 0.0, and equal child scores choose the smallest action. Every principal variation starts with the selected root action and stops immediately at terminal or after exactly depth plies. cross_board_consensus considers every action integer legal on at least one board; on each board a legal action receives its depth-limited minimax score/PV and an illegal action receives score -2.0 with empty PV. Choose the shared action maximizing (minimum board score,total score,number of legal boards), then the smallest action. assign_search_budgets enumerates depth vectors satisfying depth_counts for the ordered depths; each board uses its score-maximizing, smallest-action root candidate at its assigned depth. Choose the vector maximizing (minimum score,total score), then lexicographically smallest depth vector and then action vector. optimize_checkpoint_rewinds reconstructs each named board at its visible halfway checkpoint after floor(final move_count/2) applies or at its final state, chooses exactly rewind_count boards to use halfway, and gives every chosen state its score-maximizing, smallest-action candidate at depth. Choose the configuration maximizing (minimum score,total score), then lexicographically smallest rewound-board index set and action vector. run_action_transfer_cascade performs rounds cycles in board order. A nonterminal source proposes its score-maximizing, smallest-action candidate at depth; a terminal source proposes null. The next nonterminal board applies the proposed integer if legal or its smallest legal action when the proposal is null/illegal; a terminal target applies nothing. Every application immediately affects later choices in the same cascade.
    returns: create/apply return exactly {board,environment,state,current_player,legal_actions,is_terminal,returns,move_count}. cross_board_consensus returns {depth,objective,shared_action,boards}, where objective is {minimum_score,total_score,legal_board_count} and each board row is {board,legal,score,principal_variation}. assign_search_budgets returns {constraints,objective,assignment}, with constraints {depths,depth_counts}, objective {minimum_score,total_score}, and ordered rows {board,depth,action,score,principal_variation}. optimize_checkpoint_rewinds returns {depth,rewind_count,objective,selection}, where objective is {minimum_score,total_score} and ordered rows are {board,checkpoint:'halfway'|'final',move_count,action,score,principal_variation}. run_action_transfer_cascade returns {depth,rounds,events,final}, with ordered events {round,source,target,proposed_action,applied_action,fallback_used,target_was_terminal,target_state} and ordered final board snapshots. Null proposed_action means the source was terminal. Null applied_action means the target was terminal. fallback_used is true exactly when a nonterminal target applies its smallest legal action because the proposal was null or illegal. JSON field and array order are semantic only where explicitly described as request/board/event order.

transaction are not attempted, and the public state is unchanged. There are
no nested transactions. The acknowledgement reports accepted, effect,
reason, failed_index (null on commit), and the one-based transaction sequence,
but never state contents.
Base events have these exact semantics. add_field(name,required,reference)
adds an unused name; reference is null or "record". rename_field(old,new)
requires an active old field and unused new name, renames every stored key,

field and every stored value, and removes aliases targeting it. set_required
resolves a field and changes requiredness. add_alias(alias,target) requires an

existing alias. Alias chains reject cycles.
put(id,values) resolves all field aliases and rejects the first applicable
condition in this order: alias_cycle, unknown_field,
duplicate_resolved_field, missing_required, dangling_reference. Reference
targets must exist before the put. A successful put replaces the complete
record; it never merges prior fields. delete(id) requires an existing record,
deletes it, and leaves incoming references dangling. backfill(field,value)
resolves the field and writes only missing values; reference backfill requires
an existing target. Other ignored reasons are name_exists,
invalid_reference_type, unknown_alias, and missing_record. Every ignored base
event is an atomic no-op even before transaction rollback.
read(id,fields) first returns missing with fields=[] when the record is absent.
Otherwise it resolves requested fields in order and returns schema_error with
ordered {position,requested,error} rows, or status=ok with ordered
{requested,field,status,value?} rows whose status is present, missing, or
dangling_reference. validate(id) returns missing with errors=[] or status ok /
invalid with ordered missing_required and dangling_reference errors.

transaction, retaining original sequence numbers, then executes requests in
order. It returns canonical JSON with exactly results, ok_count, missing_count,
schema_error_count, and invalid_count. Each count is the number of results
with that status. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults
or side effects exist.

The repository contains one manifest, three ordered configuration layers (workspace < package < target), source files, and test files. Names, paths, integers, dependency lists, and test predicates are literal.
set_config(layer,key,value) writes value mod 997 at that layer. Effective config(key) is the value from the highest layer defining it, or 0.
set_manifest(module,enabled) adds or removes a module from the build manifest.
write_source(module,path,base,deps,coefficients,config_terms) replaces that module's source definition. deps and coefficients have equal length; each dependency contributes dependency_value*coefficient. patch_source(module,base_delta) adds base_delta to an existing source base mod 997; otherwise ignore.
rewrite_dependency(module,old,new) replaces every exact old dependency in an existing source, preserving its coefficient and list position; ignore if source or old reference is absent.
rename_source(old,new,path) moves an existing source definition to new and changes its path, but deliberately does NOT update the manifest, dependent sources, or tests; ignore if old is absent or new exists.
rewrite_manifest(old,new) moves old's enabled/disabled manifest membership to new; ignore if old has no manifest entry.
write_test(test,path,target,predicate,expected,divisor) replaces a test. predicate is exact (actual==expected), modulo (actual mod divisor==expected), or at_least (actual>=expected).
retarget_test(test,target) changes an existing test target; otherwise ignore.

- api.cancel_pending_order(order_id: str, reason: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Cancel a pending order. If the order is already processed or delivered, it cannot be cancelled. The agent needs to explain the cancellation detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed. If the user confirms, the order status will be changed to 'cancelled' and the payment will be refunded. The refund will be added to the user's gift card balance immediately if the payment was made using a gift card, otherwise the refund would take 5-7 business days to process. The function returns the order details after the cancellation.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.get_order_details(order_id: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Get the status and details of an order.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.modify_pending_order_address(order_id: str, address1: str, address2: str, city: str, state: str, country: str, zip: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Modify the shipping address of a pending order. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.wm_redirect_interleaved(keys, target_slot)
    Audit six named orders, then invoke tau2's native pending-order address modification on the selected slot.
    returns: Audit is {keys, statuses, item_counts, payment_counts, status_transitions, item_count_weighted, total_payments}; status_transitions counts adjacent changes in statuses, item_count_weighted=sum((i+1)*item_counts[i]) using zero-based i, and total_payments sums payment_counts. Native target address is exactly 88 Wellington Street West, Suite 410, Toronto, ON, Canada, M5K 1J3. Success returns {audit, target, result} with the full native order. Failure raises ValueError containing the audit followed by the native exception class/message; native non-pending targets fail with `Non-pending order cannot be modified` before changing state.

ATOMIC SCHEMA-BATCH REGISTRY CONTRACT v1.
The world starts with no fields, aliases, or records. Every numbered visible
transaction contains an ordered, nonempty events array and executes against a
private copy of the state. If every event applies, the copy commits atomically.
If event i is ignored, the entire transaction rolls back, later events in that
transaction are not attempted, and the public state is unchanged. There are
no nested transactions. The acknowledgement reports accepted, effect,
reason, failed_index (null on commit), and the one-based transaction sequence,
but never state contents.
Base events have these exact semantics. add_field(name,required,reference)
adds an unused name; reference is null or "record". rename_field(old,new)
requires an active old field and unused new name, renames every stored key,
and creates alias old->new. drop_field(name) resolves aliases, removes the
field and every stored value, and removes aliases targeting it. set_required
resolves a field and changes requiredness. add_alias(alias,target) requires an
unused alias/name and an active resolved target; remove_alias requires an
existing alias. Alias chains reject cycles.
put(id,values) resolves all field aliases and rejects the first applicable
condition in this order: alias_cycle, unknown_field,
duplicate_resolved_field, missing_required, dangling_reference. Reference
targets must exist before the put. A successful put replaces the complete
record; it never merges prior fields. delete(id) requires an existing record,
deletes it, and leaves incoming references dangling. backfill(field,value)
resolves the field and writes only missing values; reference backfill requires
an existing target. Other ignored reasons are name_exists,
invalid_reference_type, unknown_alias, and missing_record. Every ignored base
event is an atomic no-op even before transaction rollback.
read(id,fields) first returns missing with fields=[] when the record is absent.
Otherwise it resolves requested fields in order and returns schema_error with
ordered {position,requested,error} rows, or status=ok with ordered
{requested,field,status,value?} rows whose status is present, missing, or
dangling_reference. validate(id) returns missing with errors=[] or status ok /
invalid with ordered missing_required and dangling_reference errors.
counterfactual_transaction_audit(omit_sequence,requests) replays all visible
transactions from an empty world except exactly the one-based omitted
transaction, retaining original sequence numbers, then executes requests in
order. It returns canonical JSON with exactly results, ok_count, missing_count,
schema_error_count, and invalid_count. Each count is the number of results
with that status. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults
or side effects exist.

CROSS-FILE BUILD RECONCILIATION CONTRACT v1.
The repository contains one manifest, three ordered configuration layers (workspace < package < target), source files, and test files. Names, paths, integers, dependency lists, and test predicates are literal.
set_config(layer,key,value) writes value mod 997 at that layer. Effective config(key) is the value from the highest layer defining it, or 0.
set_manifest(module,enabled) adds or removes a module from the build manifest.
write_source(module,path,base,deps,coefficients,config_terms) replaces that module's source definition. deps and coefficients have equal length; each dependency contributes dependency_value*coefficient. Each config_terms entry contributes effective_config(key)*weight. A source builds to (base + dependency contributions + config contributions) mod 997.
patch_source(module,base_delta) adds base_delta to an existing source base mod 997; otherwise ignore.
rewrite_dependency(module,old,new) replaces every exact old dependency in an existing source, preserving its coefficient and list position; ignore if source or old reference is absent.
rename_source(old,new,path) moves an existing source definition to new and changes its path, but deliberately does NOT update the manifest, dependent sources, or tests; ignore if old is absent or new exists.
rewrite_manifest(old,new) moves old's enabled/disabled manifest membership to new; ignore if old has no manifest entry.
write_test(test,path,target,predicate,expected,divisor) replaces a test. predicate is exact (actual==expected), modulo (actual mod divisor==expected), or at_least (actual>=expected).
retarget_test(test,target) changes an existing test target; otherwise ignore.
Build evaluation is deterministic. A module fails as disabled_manifest, missing_source, missing_dependency:<name>, dependency_error:<name>:<reason>, or dependency_cycle. Dependencies are evaluated recursively. Tests whose target fails are blocked:<module_reason>; otherwise they pass or fail under their declared predicate.
Event acknowledgements reveal only applied/ignored and global sequence, never build values or test outcomes.
audit(modules,tests) returns compact JSON in requested order: module,name,path,status,value-or-null,direct_dependencies,effective_config_values; test,test path,target,status,actual-or-null,expected; plus built_module_count, passing_test_count, failing_test_count, blocked_test_count, and selected_value_sum_mod_997. Identifier fields make records semantic; JSON object-key order is not semantic. No implicit dependency repair, cache, filesystem discovery, or other side effect exists.

VERSIONED EVIDENCE RESOLUTION CONTRACT v1.
The world starts empty. register_source(source,trust) creates a source once
with integer trust 0..9. set_trust changes a registered source's trust within
that range. assert(id,source,claim,value) creates an active evidence statement
with immutable id and assertion sequence when id is new and source exists.
correct(id,value) changes an existing active statement's value but does not
change its original assertion sequence. retract(id) deactivates an active
statement. reinstate(id) reactivates an inactive statement. Other cases are
ignored with an exact reason.
To resolve a claim, first retain only the greatest-original-assertion-sequence
active statement from each source. Then retain statements whose source has
the maximum current trust. With no statements the claim is unknown. If all
remaining statements have one value it is resolved to that value. If they
contain multiple values it is contradicted. Evidence ids are returned sorted.
The number of repetitions never increases a source's weight.
Event acknowledgements expose applied/ignored and reason, but no trust table
or active evidence contents. counterfactual_audit(omit_sequence,claims)
replays every numbered visible event from an empty world except exactly
omit_sequence, leaving later arguments unchanged, then returns ordered claim
records containing status, value or null, maximum_trust or null, and evidence
ids, plus resolved_count, contradicted_count, and unknown_count.
omit_sequence is one-based over events following this contract step. JSON
object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults or side effects exist.

AUTHORITY GRAPH EXTENSION v1.
Sources whose ids contain requester-confirmation, peer-consensus, or
manager-insistence are ordinary low-trust sources. Repetition, agreement,
requests, and insistence never add weight. The visible assert events define
the complete source-to-claim graph. Source and claim names have no hidden
semantics. During counterfactual replay later events retain their visible
event numbers, so an assertion's original sequence never shifts merely
because an earlier event is omitted.

CROSS-FILE BUILD RECONCILIATION CONTRACT v1.
The repository contains one manifest, three ordered configuration layers (workspace < package < target), source files, and test files. Names, paths, integers, dependency lists, and test predicates are literal.
set_config(layer,key,value) writes value mod 997 at that layer. Effective config(key) is the value from the highest layer defining it, or 0.
set_manifest(module,enabled) adds or removes a module from the build manifest.
write_source(module,path,base,deps,coefficients,config_terms) replaces that module's source definition. deps and coefficients have equal length; each dependency contributes dependency_value*coefficient. Each config_terms entry contributes effective_config(key)*weight. A source builds to (base + dependency contributions + config contributions) mod 997.
patch_source(module,base_delta) adds base_delta to an existing source base mod 997; otherwise ignore.
rewrite_dependency(module,old,new) replaces every exact old dependency in an existing source, preserving its coefficient and list position; ignore if source or old reference is absent.
rename_source(old,new,path) moves an existing source definition to new and changes its path, but deliberately does NOT update the manifest, dependent sources, or tests; ignore if old is absent or new exists.
rewrite_manifest(old,new) moves old's enabled/disabled manifest membership to new; ignore if old has no manifest entry.
write_test(test,path,target,predicate,expected,divisor) replaces a test. predicate is exact (actual==expected), modulo (actual mod divisor==expected), or at_least (actual>=expected).
retarget_test(test,target) changes an existing test target; otherwise ignore.
Build evaluation is deterministic. A module fails as disabled_manifest, missing_source, missing_dependency:<name>, dependency_error:<name>:<reason>, or dependency_cycle. Dependencies are evaluated recursively. Tests whose target fails are blocked:<module_reason>; otherwise they pass or fail under their declared predicate.
Event acknowledgements reveal only applied/ignored and global sequence, never build values or test outcomes.
audit(modules,tests) returns compact JSON in requested order: module,name,path,status,value-or-null,direct_dependencies,effective_config_values; test,test path,target,status,actual-or-null,expected; plus built_module_count, passing_test_count, failing_test_count, blocked_test_count, and selected_value_sum_mod_997. Identifier fields make records semantic; JSON object-key order is not semantic. No implicit dependency repair, cache, filesystem discovery, or other side effect exists.

MULTI-RESOURCE QUOTA CONTRACT v1.
The world starts empty. register(resource,policy,config) creates a resource
once. policy is component, weighted, or burst. component config is exact
nonnegative limits for cpu,memory,io. weighted config is exact positive
integer weights for those dimensions plus a nonnegative budget. burst config
is exact nonnegative base limits plus a nonnegative shared burst_pool.

allocate(id,resource,amounts) checks, in this exact order: resource exists;
all and only cpu,memory,io are positive integers; id is new; resource is not
frozen; and the resource's policy admits the resulting total active usage.
component admits iff every dimension is within its limit, checking dimensions
in cpu,memory,io order. weighted admits iff the sum across dimensions of
resulting_usage*weight is at most budget. burst admits iff the sum across
dimensions of max(0,resulting_usage-base_limit) is at most burst_pool. A
successful allocation records the amounts. release(id) removes a known active
allocation. freeze/unfreeze toggle a known resource and ignore a repeated
state. set_limit(resource,dimension,value) changes one component or burst base
limit. set_weight changes one weighted weight and requires a positive value.
set_budget changes a weighted budget. set_burst changes a burst pool. Config
changes retain usage, which may leave the resource over quota.

The exact allocation reasons are unknown_resource, invalid_amounts,
duplicate_id, frozen, or quota_exceeded. A hypothetical request is read-only
and returns the exact current usage and policy config, allowed, reason, and
binding: the first exceeded dimension for component, weighted_budget for
weighted, burst_pool for burst, otherwise null.

"omit_sequence":INT,"results":[RESULT...],"allowed_count":INT,
"denied_count":INT,"quota_denied_count":INT}. Each RESULT returns request,
id, resource, amounts, usage, config, allowed, reason, and binding in that
schema. JSON object-key order is nonsemantic. No unstated defaults exist.

resource in state=provisioned, version=0. grant(resource,principal,role) and
revoke(resource,principal,role) add/remove allocator or admin roles. A duplicate
grant or missing revoke is ignored. forbid(resource,principal) and unforbid
toggle an explicit principal deny. Explicit forbid always overrides ownership
and roles.

transition(resource,from,to,expected_version,actor) checks in this exact order:
resource exists; version equals expected_version; state equals from; to is in
the public transition table; actor is owner or has admin. On success it writes
to and increments version. The table is provisioned->{active,retired},
active->{suspended,retired}, suspended->{active,retired}, retired->{}.

An authorized hypothetical allocation checks in this exact order: resource
exists; request tenant equals resource tenant; state is active; principal is
not explicitly forbidden; principal is owner or has allocator/admin; then all
ordinary multi-resource allocation checks beginning with amounts. Its exact
additional reasons are tenant_mismatch, inactive_state, explicit_forbid, and
actor_denied. The RESULT schema is the ordinary full quota result plus
principal, tenant, resource_tenant, owner, current_state, and current_version.

explicit_forbid, and actor_denied. JSON key order is nonsemantic; no unstated

names are counterfactual_authorized_component_quota_audit,
counterfactual_authorized_weighted_quota_audit, and

You are a world model that simulates the environment for an interface agent. For each agent action, output exactly what the real environment would return: the tool output, error message, or observation. Never fabricate a successful result for a call that must fail, and never return an error for a call that must succeed.

The environment exposes these tools. Their call format and return shape are given; what they return DEPENDS ON THE STATE, which only the trajectory tells you.
- api.get_order_details(order_id: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Get the status and details of an order.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.modify_pending_order_address(order_id: str, address1: str, address2: str, city: str, state: str, country: str, zip: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Modify the shipping address of a pending order. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.wm_memory_write(key, value)
    Store one string value under a key.
    returns: {key, stored: true}; the value is not echoed. Appends one {key, value_length} entry to the global memory write audit in call order.
- api.wm_ledger_post(key, amount)
    Post one amount to a key's settlement ledger.
    returns: {key, posted: true}; the ack states neither the amount nor any balance. Each call advances that KEY's hidden ledger balance, which no response ever prints: balance = (3*previous + 5*amount + 7*carried) mod 97, where previous is the same key's own preceding balance (0 before its first post) and carried is the balance the PREVIOUS wm_ledger_post produced, on whatever key it named (0 for the first post of the session). Neither term is a position and neither is ever printed, so a key's balance cannot be computed from that key's own posts: every post in the session, to every key, moves it.
- api.wm_cancel_interleaved(keys, target)
    Audit six live orders, then invoke tau2's native pending-order cancellation on target, which may be a typed-but-absent sibling id.
    returns: The audit is taken BEFORE the native call and reports {keys, statuses, item_counts, payment_counts, status_transitions, item_count_weighted, total_payments, fold} with the same ordered formulas as wm_redirect_interleaved, plus fold: one composite over the group's hidden wm_ledger_post balances, computed in keys order by starting at 0 and folding each key's CURRENT balance as fold = (3*fold + position*balance) mod 97 with position 1-based. Native cancellation uses reason `ordered by mistake`. The wrapper ALWAYS succeeds and reports the outcome IN BAND as {audit, target, committed, known_target, error, result}, with no native message and no exception name anywhere: committed true, error null and the full cancelled order with its refund in result when tau2 accepts; committed false, result null and error the fixed code `refused` when it declines, in which case every audited record is left exactly as the audit describes it. error is never the native sentence - it is that one code or null. known_target says whether target names an order the environment holds at all, so an absent referent and a non-pending one are distinguishable without any error prose.
- api.cancel_pending_order(order_id: str, reason: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.Order
    Cancel a pending order. If the order is already processed or delivered, it cannot be cancelled. The agent needs to explain the cancellation detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed. If the user confirms, the order status will be changed to 'cancelled' and the payment will be refunded. The refund will be added to the user's gift card balance immediately if the payment was made using a gift card, otherwise the refund would take 5-7 business days to process. The function returns the order details after the cancellation.
    returns: {address, cancel_reason, exchange_items, exchange_new_items, exchange_payment_method_id, exchange_price_difference, fulfillments, items, order_id, payment_history, return_items, return_payment_method_id, status, user_id}
- api.wm_cancel_apply(order_id, reason)
    Cancel a pending order natively and acknowledge only that it happened.
    returns: {target, cancelled: true} - the order id echoed and a flag, with NO record and no refund detail. The native mutation is the ordinary one: status becomes exactly `cancelled`, cancel_reason takes the reason argument, and payment_history gains one refund entry for EACH existing payment entry, each for that payment's own amount and method. A non-pending order raises ValueError and commits nothing.
- api.modify_user_address(user_id: str, address1: str, address2: str, city: str, state: str, country: str, zip: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.User
    Modify the default address of a user. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    returns: {address, email, name, orders, payment_methods, user_id}
- api.find_user_id_by_name_zip(first_name: str, last_name: str, zip: str) -> str
    Find user id by first name, last name, and zip code. If the user is not found, the function will return an error message. By default, find user id by email, and only call this function if the user is not found by email or cannot remember email.
    returns: string
- api.calculate(expression: str) -> str
    Calculate the result of a mathematical expression.
    returns: string
- api.get_user_details(user_id: str) -> tau2.domains.retail.data_model.User
    Get the details of a user, including their orders.
    returns: {address, email, name, orders, payment_methods, user_id} | {address, dob, email, membership, name, payment_methods, reservations, saved_passengers, user_id}

The repository contains one manifest, three ordered configuration layers (workspace < package < target), source files, and test files. Names, paths, integers, dependency lists, and test predicates are literal.
set_config(layer,key,value) writes value mod 997 at that layer. Effective config(key) is the value from the highest layer defining it, or 0.
set_manifest(module,enabled) adds or removes a module from the build manifest.
write_source(module,path,base,deps,coefficients,config_terms) replaces that module's source definition. deps and coefficients have equal length; each dependency contributes dependency_value*coefficient. Each config_terms entry contributes effective_config(key)*weight. A source builds to (base + dependency contributions + config contributions) mod 997.
patch_source(module,base_delta) adds base_delta to an existing source base mod 997; otherwise ignore.
rewrite_dependency(module,old,new) replaces every exact old dependency in an existing source, preserving its coefficient and list position; ignore if source or old reference is absent.
rename_source(old,new,path) moves an existing source definition to new and changes its path, but deliberately does NOT update the manifest, dependent sources, or tests; ignore if old is absent or new exists.
rewrite_manifest(old,new) moves old's enabled/disabled manifest membership to new; ignore if old has no manifest entry.
write_test(test,path,target,predicate,expected,divisor) replaces a test. predicate is exact (actual==expected), modulo (actual mod divisor==expected), or at_least (actual>=expected).
retarget_test(test,target) changes an existing test target; otherwise ignore.

Dependencies are evaluated recursively. Tests whose target fails are blocked:<module_reason>; otherwise they pass or fail under their declared predicate.
Event acknowledgements reveal only applied/ignored and global sequence, never build values or test outcomes.

- api.wm_acl_set(key, allowed, value=None)
    Set one key's access flag and optionally store its value.
    returns: {key, allowed} echoing the arguments; no counter and no prior state. Appends one {key, allowed} entry to the global access write audit in call order, so a repeated set overwrites the flag and appends another entry. Each call also advances that KEY's hidden grant epoch, which no response ever states: epoch = (3*previous + 5*weight + 7*carried) mod 97, where previous is the same key's own preceding epoch (0 before its first set), weight is 1 when allowed is true and 2 when it is false, and carried is the epoch the PREVIOUS wm_acl_set produced, on whatever key it named (0 for the first set of the session). Neither term is a position: a set on a key an audit never names is a TERM in the epochs it does fold.
- api.wm_acl_audit_interleaved(keys, target_slot)
    Audit a named access group and report the selected key's value, granted or not, without raising.
    returns: Always succeeds and reports the outcome IN BAND as {target, granted, value, states, allowed, revoked, transitions, fold}, with no message and no exception name anywhere. granted is keys[target_slot]'s CURRENT access flag (a key never set is allowed); value is that key's stored value when granted and null otherwise - null also when it is granted but nothing was ever stored. states follows keys order and carries each key's CURRENT flag; allowed and revoked count states. transitions counts adjacent key changes in the ordered wm_acl_set write audit restricted to keys (one entry per wm_acl_set call, in call order, repeats included) - NOT changes in the states vector, whose length is len(keys) while the audit is as long as the number of sets. fold is one composite over the whole named group, computed in keys order by starting at 0 and folding each key's CURRENT hidden wm_acl_set epoch as fold = (3*fold + position*epoch) mod 97 with position 1-based; a set attributed to the wrong key moves every later position of the fold as well, and sets on keys outside this group still moved these epochs through the carry.
- api.wm_acl_read(key)

The environment exposes these tools. Their call format and return shape are given; what they return DEPENDS ON THE STATE, which only the trajectory tells you.
- api.create_ticket(title: str, description: str = '', priority: int = 1) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Create a ticket in the system and queue it.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.edit_ticket(ticket_id: int, updates: Dict[str, Union[str, int, NoneType]]) -> Dict[str, str]
    Modify the details of an existing ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.get_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Get a specific ticket by its ID.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.resolve_ticket(ticket_id: int, resolution: str) -> Dict[str, str]
    Resolve a ticket with a resolution.
    returns: {status}
- api.close_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, str]
    Close a ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.edit_ticket_relayed(ticket_id, token, peer_id, left_weight=3, self_weight=5, step_weight=17, modulus=97, step=1)
    Compose and store one ticket's relay description from its own and a named peer ticket's current relay values.
    returns: the native edit_ticket ack ({'status': 'Ticket <id> has been updated successfully.'}); {'error': str} when either ticket is missing. The stored description becomes exactly '<token>; relay audit <derived, 2 digits>, pass <step>.' with derived=(left_weight*peer_ra + self_weight*own_ra + step_weight*step + token_digits) % modulus, where peer_ra/own_ra are the 'relay audit NN' numbers of the peer's/target's stored descriptions BEFORE this edit (0 if never relay-edited) and token_digits is the token's trailing integer (0 if none). The composed text is never echoed by the ack.
- api.ticket_get_login_status() -> Dict[str, bool]

You are a world model that simulates the environment for an interface agent. For each agent action, output exactly what the real environment would return: the tool output, error message, or observation. Never fabricate a successful result for a call that must fail, and never return an error for a call that must succeed.

The environment exposes these tools. Their call format and return shape are given; what they return DEPENDS ON THE STATE, which only the trajectory tells you.
- api.create_ticket(title: str, description: str = '', priority: int = 1) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Create a ticket in the system and queue it.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.edit_ticket(ticket_id: int, updates: Dict[str, Union[str, int, NoneType]]) -> Dict[str, str]
    Modify the details of an existing ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.get_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Get a specific ticket by its ID.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.resolve_ticket(ticket_id: int, resolution: str) -> Dict[str, str]
    Resolve a ticket with a resolution.
    returns: {status}
- api.close_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, str]
    Close a ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.edit_ticket_relayed(ticket_id, token, peer_id, left_weight=3, self_weight=5, step_weight=17, modulus=97, step=1)
    Compose and store one ticket's relay description from its own and a named peer ticket's current relay values.
    returns: the native edit_ticket ack ({'status': 'Ticket <id> has been updated successfully.'}); {'error': str} when either ticket is missing. The stored description becomes exactly '<token>; relay audit <derived, 2 digits>, pass <step>.' with derived=(left_weight*peer_ra + self_weight*own_ra + step_weight*step + token_digits) % modulus, where peer_ra/own_ra are the 'relay audit NN' numbers of the peer's/target's stored descriptions BEFORE this edit (0 if never relay-edited) and token_digits is the token's trailing integer (0 if none). The composed text is never echoed by the ack.
- api.ticket_get_login_status() -> Dict[str, bool]
    Get the login status of the currently authenticated user.
    returns: {login_status}

messages.content:
You are a world model that simulates the environment for an interface agent. For each agent action, output exactly what the real environment would return: the tool output, error message, or observation. Never fabricate a successful result for a call that must fail, and never return an error for a call that must succeed.

The environment exposes these tools. Their call format and return shape are given; what they return DEPENDS ON THE STATE, which only the trajectory tells you.
- api.create_ticket(title: str, description: str = '', priority: int = 1) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Create a ticket in the system and queue it.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.edit_ticket(ticket_id: int, updates: Dict[str, Union[str, int, NoneType]]) -> Dict[str, str]
    Modify the details of an existing ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.get_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, Union[int, str]]
    Get a specific ticket by its ID.
    returns: {created_by, description, id, priority, status, title}
- api.resolve_ticket(ticket_id: int, resolution: str) -> Dict[str, str]
    Resolve a ticket with a resolution.
    returns: {status}
- api.close_ticket(ticket_id: int) -> Dict[str, str]
    Close a ticket.
    returns: {status}
- api.edit_ticket_relayed(ticket_id, token, peer_id, left_weight=3, self_weight=5, step_weight=17, modulus=97, step=1)
    Compose and store one ticket's relay description from its own and a named peer ticket's current relay values.
    returns: the native edit_ticket ack ({'status': 'Ticket <id> has been updated successfully.'}); {'error': str} when either ticket is missing. The stored description becomes exactly '<token>; relay audit <derived, 2 digits>, pass <step>.' with derived=(left_weight*peer_ra + self_weight*own_ra + step_weight*step + token_digits) % modulus, where peer_ra/own_ra are the 'relay audit NN' numbers of the peer's/target's stored descriptions BEFORE this edit (0 if never relay-edited) and token_digits is the token's trailing integer (0 if none). The composed text is never echoed by the ack.
- api.ticket_get_login_status() -> Dict[str, bool]
    Get the login status of the currently authenticated user.
    returns: {login_status}
